summary: Wooden light on the government wharf near the west end of Pictou Island, put in operation in 1907; not the 1905 west-point light.

access.note: Site open, tower closed. Reached by passenger ferry from Caribou on a varying schedule, May through November.

keepers.name: Charles D. Patterson
keepers.note: Appointed 29 March 1905 (1906-07 table, printed p.174, and 1908-09 table, printed p.179, read on page images). Listed as 'West End of Pictou Island' in 1906-07, 'Pictou Island Pier, west end' in 1908-09 and 1910-11, and 'Pictou island, W.E' in 1912-13. LighthouseFriends, writing about the west-end light, names him first keeper at $400 a year and says he retired in 1933. Whether the 1908-11 'Pier, west end' entries name the wharf light or the west-end light is not settled by the sources read.

keepers.name: Hugh McLean
keepers.note: Second name on the line under 'Pictou Island Pier, west end' in the 1908-09 and 1910-11 tables (ditto station mark). Appointed 24 June 1905 at $100. The tables give no role. Matched by position; checked on the 1908-09 and 1910-11 page images. Not identified with J. McLean of 1911.

keepers.name: J. McLean
keepers.note: Listed against 'Pictou island wharf' in the 1912-13 table, appointed 22 December 1911 at $120 (printed p.62, read by position, checked on the page image). Printed with initial and surname only; not identified with Hugh McLean (1905) on any source read.

corrections.why: The 1905 date belongs to the light on the west point (1905-06 report). The wharf light the record describes was put in operation in 1907 (1907-08 report).
The 1907-08 report gives the tower as 26 feet high to the top of the ventilator, which is 7.9 m. The Lighthouse Directory gives 8 m (27 ft).

The 14 m focal plane in the record is the west-point light's figure. The Lighthouse Directory gives the wharf light a focal plane of 11 m (35 ft). The 1907-08 report gives 32 ft above high water (9.8 m) for the light as first built; the two may differ by datum or by a later change.

The Lighthouse Directory describes the wharf light as white, 2 s on and 2 s off, which is an isophase 4 s character. The record's LFl W 6s is not the wharf light's described character. Check against the CCG List of Lights before applying.
CAN381 is the west-point light's number in the Lighthouse Directory. The wharf light is ARLHS CAN-380.
A897 is the west-point light in the CCG list. The Lighthouse Directory gives the wharf light as CCG A-899.
H1244 is the west-point light in the CCG list. The Lighthouse Directory gives the wharf light as Admiralty H1237.
8612 is the west-point light's NGA number in the Lighthouse Directory. The wharf light is NGA 8608.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1905 date, its 1965 tower date and its position and aton numbers belong to the light on the west point. The wharf light was put in operation in 1907 (1907-08 report). LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory describe the west-point light under the name Pictou Island West End.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27 (independent pass). Changes: (1) The story no longer says 'some listings give 1905' (no listing read gives 1905 for the wharf light; the Lighthouse Directory gives 1907). The 1905 date belongs to the west-end light (1905-06 report; Directory 'Pictou Island West End', 'station established 1905'). (2) Patterson's appointment is 29 March 1905, not 1908. Checked on page images: 1906-07 table (printed p.174, 'West End of Pictou Island'), 1908-09 table (printed p.179, 'Pictou Island Pier, west end'), 1910-11 table (printed p.257) and 1912-13 table (printed p.62, 'Pictou island, W.E'). The OCR of the 1910-11 table reads 'Mar. 20, lOitS'; the image reads 29 March 1905. (3) Hugh McLean (24 June 1905, $100) is on the line under Patterson in the 1908-09 and 1910-11 tables (ditto station mark) and is added to the roster with role 'other'. (4) The 1912-13 table (printed p.62, scan 69) names a keeper for the wharf light: J. McLean, appointed 22 December 1911 at $120. The earlier draft said the sources did not show who kept the wharf light after 1911. Patterson is at 'Pictou island, W.E' in that table. (5) The 1912-13 page is a statement of light stations and keepers, not a station list. Its three Pictou entries are 'Pictou island S.E' (A. McFarlane), 'Pictou island, W.E' (C. D. Patterson) and 'Pictou island wharf' (J. McLean). (6) Units: the story now gives metres first (7.9 m (26 ft), 9.8 m (32 ft), 8.0 m by 6.4 m (26 ft 4 in by 20 ft 10 in)). (7) The 1907-08 entry is described as the 1907-08 report, not 'the 1907 season'. (8) 'The keeper's house followed' is softened: the 1907-08 phrase is 'the keeper of the west pier lighthouse', and the reports do not say which light the 1908-09 dwelling served. (9) Open: whether 'Pictou Island Pier, west end' (1908-11) means the wharf light or the west-end light; whether Patterson kept one light or both. The sources read here do not settle either. A human should decide. (10) Not checked: the Directory of Federal Heritage Designations page for Pictou Island South (id 14894), as noted in the earlier draft; the Pictou Island 'Life-Saving station' (a separate station; see the earlier note). (11) Owner and agency are left null, as before. CCG List of Lights (source 9) is cited in evidence but not in the story; the H1237 and A899 identifiers are from the Directory.
